es: Distinguir entre contar una emoción y mostrarla con acciones y detalles de los sentidos, y repasar used to y would para hábitos del pasado.

teaching.en: Her hands began to tremble as she opened the letter.

teaching.explanationEs: Muestra el nervio con una reacción del cuerpo, sin decir «she was nervous».
segments: Her hands began to tremble
as she opened the letter.
teaching.audioText: Her hands began to tremble as she opened the letter.

teaching.en: He slammed the door so hard that the glasses on the shelf rattled.
teaching.es: Dio un portazo tan fuerte que los vasos de la estantería tintinearon.
teaching.explanationEs: La acción y el sonido muestran la rabia sin nombrarla.
segments: He slammed the door so hard that
the glasses on the shelf rattled.
teaching.audioText: He slammed the door so hard that the glasses on the shelf rattled.

teaching.en: The smell of burnt milk filled the kitchen, and nobody said a word.
teaching.es: El olor a leche quemada llenó la cocina y nadie dijo una palabra.
teaching.explanationEs: Un detalle del olfato y el silencio muestran la tensión.
segments: The smell of burnt milk filled the
kitchen, and nobody said a word.
teaching.audioText: The smell of burnt milk filled the kitchen, and nobody said a word.

teaching.en: When we were kids, we would sit on the wall every evening and count the cars.
teaching.es: De pequeños, nos sentábamos en el muro cada tarde y contábamos los coches.
teaching.explanationEs: Would + verbo describe una acción que se repetía en el pasado.
segments: When we were kids, we would sit on
the wall every evening and count the cars.
teaching.audioText: When we were kids, we would sit on the wall every evening and count the cars.

teaching.en: The old house used to smell of pine and wet wool.
teaching.es: La casa vieja solía oler a pino y a lana mojada.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to sirve para estados y hábitos del pasado; para estados no se usa would.
segments: The old house used to smell
of pine and wet wool.
teaching.audioText: The old house used to smell of pine and wet wool.

teaching.en: She bit her nails and checked the clock every minute.
teaching.es: Se mordía las uñas y miraba el reloj cada minuto.
teaching.explanationEs: Dos acciones concretas muestran la ansiedad; contar sería «she was anxious».
segments: She bit her nails and
checked the clock every minute.
teaching.audioText: She bit her nails and checked the clock every minute.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase muestra el miedo en lugar de nombrarlo?

choices.text: She locked the door and put a chair against it.
She was terrified.
She felt a lot of fear.

feedback.es: Cerrar la puerta con llave y poner una silla contra ella son acciones que el lector ve y le hacen deducir el miedo. Las otras dos lo nombran.

hint.es: Busca acciones que el lector podría ver.

prompt.es: Completa: «Le temblaban las manos de rabia.»

answer.text: with

feedback.es: La causa de una reacción del cuerpo se introduce con with: shaking with anger.

hint.es: Es la preposición que introduce la causa de una reacción.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta sobre un estado del pasado.

choices.text: We would live near the sea.
We used to live near the sea.
We were used to live near the sea.

feedback.es: Live es un estado, y los estados del pasado usan used to. Would no se usa con estados y were used to live no existe.

hint.es: Vivir en un lugar es un estado, no una acción repetida.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la emoción que muestra.

pairs: He tapped his foot and kept looking at the door.
She hugged the old coat and closed her eyes.
The room went silent when he walked in.
He jumped out of his chair and shouted the news.

feedback.es: Cada frase da una acción concreta: golpear el suelo con el pie y mirar la puerta (impaciencia), abrazar el abrigo (nostalgia), silencio al entrar (tensión) y saltar de la silla (alegría).

pairs: He tapped his foot and kept looking at the door.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué detalle muestra el miedo del perro.

choices.text: The rain is loud.
The roof is old.
The dog goes under the table.

feedback.es: El perro se esconde debajo de la mesa: es una acción que muestra el miedo. La lluvia y el tejado son solo ambiente.

origin.audio: The rain was loud, and the dog hid under the table.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cada verano contábamos los barcos del río.»

answer.text: Every summer we would count the boats on the river

feedback.es: Would + verbo base describe una acción que se repetía cada verano.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase muestra el enfado sin nombrarlo?

choices.text: He moved his chair back so hard that it fell over.
He was very angry with her.
He felt angry and upset.

feedback.es: Echar la silla atrás tan fuerte que cae es una acción visible que muestra el enfado. Las otras dos lo nombran (angry).

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la parte que muestra la emoción sin nombrarla.

choices.text: The sentence saying she was excited.
Her bright eyes and constant smile.
Sara's new school.

feedback.es: Los ojos brillantes y la sonrisa constante muestran la emoción; «Sara was excited» solo la nombra.

origin.audio: Sara was excited. Her eyes were bright, and she could not stop smiling.

prompt.es: Reescribe las dos frases mostrando la emoción con una acción o una reacción.

answer.text: Tom slammed the door so hard that the glasses rattled. Sara bit her nails and her hands began to tremble.
accepted: Tom slammed the door so hard that the glasses rattled. Sara bit her nails and her hands began to tremble.
Tom threw his phone on the table and shouted. Sara's hands shook and she checked the clock every minute.
Tom moved his chair back so hard that it fell over. Sara bit her nails and looked at the door again and again.

feedback.es: Mostrar es dar una acción o una reacción concreta: Tom portazo o golpe; Sara uñas, manos temblando o mirar el reloj. No digas angry ni nervous.

origin.text: Frases que cuentan: «Tom was angry. Sara was nervous.» Reescríbelas mostrando cada emoción con una acción o una reacción del cuerpo (sin usar angry ni nervous).

prompt.es: Completa tres detalles de una escena: un estado, un hábito y una causa.

answer.text: used | would | with

feedback.es: Used to sirve para el estado (live), would para la acción repetida (walk) y with introduce la causa del temblor.

sentences: When I was a child, we ___ to have a dog.
Every Sunday, we ___ walk to the lake.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase cuenta la emoción en lugar de mostrarla?

choices.text: He jumped up and shouted the news across the room.
He ran to tell his mother the news.
He was very happy about the news.

feedback.es: «He was very happy about the news» nombra la emoción (cuenta). Saltar de la silla y gritar la noticia la muestra.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué describe un hábito de acciones repetidas.

choices.text: The children often sat on the wall in the evenings.
The house had a smell of pine.
The children were very young.

feedback.es: «We would sit on the wall every evening» describe una acción repetida; el olor de la casa es un estado con used to.

origin.audio: When we were kids, we would sit on the wall every evening. The old house used to smell of pine.

prompt.es: Detecta la frase con un error de hábito pasado.

choices.text: We used to live in Leeds when I was a child.
We would live in Leeds when I was a child.
We would play in the street every evening.

feedback.es: Live es un estado y no admite would: debe ser used to live. Would sí vale para acciones repetidas como jugar en la calle.

es: Controlar el ritmo narrativo con anteposición de lugar (Down the hill ran the dog), Never + inversión, fragmentos intencionales y frases de longitud variada.

teaching.en: Down the hill ran the dog.
teaching.es: Colina abajo corrió el perro.
teaching.explanationEs: Anteposición: lugar + verbo + sujeto. El sujeto es un nombre (the dog).
segments: Down the hill
ran the dog.
teaching.audioText: Down the hill ran the dog.

teaching.en: On the table lay a single letter.
teaching.es: Sobre la mesa había una sola carta.
teaching.explanationEs: Con verbos como lay, stood o hung la inversión es natural: lugar + verbo + sujeto.
segments: On the table lay
a single letter.
teaching.audioText: On the table lay a single letter.

teaching.en: Down the hill it ran, barking at the wind.
teaching.es: Colina abajo corrió, ladrando al viento.
teaching.explanationEs: Si el sujeto es un pronombre no hay inversión: lugar + pronombre + verbo.
segments: Down the hill it ran,
barking at the wind.
teaching.audioText: Down the hill it ran, barking at the wind.

teaching.en: Never had she seen such a silent street.
teaching.es: Nunca había visto una calle tan silenciosa.
teaching.explanationEs: Never al inicio pide inversión: never + auxiliar + sujeto (had she).
segments: Never had she seen
such a silent street.
teaching.audioText: Never had she seen such a silent street.

teaching.en: Silence. Then footsteps. Slowly, the door opened.
teaching.es: Silencio. Luego, pasos. Despacio, la puerta se abrió.
teaching.explanationEs: Los fragmentos sin verbo crean tensión; úsalos pocas veces y con intención.
segments: Silence. Then footsteps. Slowly,
the door opened.
teaching.audioText: Silence. Then footsteps. Slowly, the door opened.

teaching.en: She walked for hours through the empty streets, past closed shops and dark windows, until the cold reached her bones. Then she stopped.
teaching.es: Caminó durante horas por las calles vacías, junto a tiendas cerradas y ventanas oscuras, hasta que el frío le llegó a los huesos. Entonces se detuvo.
teaching.explanationEs: Una frase larga que fluye y una corta que golpea crean ritmo.
segments: She walked for hours through the empty streets, past closed shops and
dark windows, until the cold reached her bones. Then she stopped.
teaching.audioText: She walked for hours through the empty streets, past closed shops and dark windows, until the cold reached her bones. Then she stopped.

feedback.es: El lugar va primero, después el verbo y al final el sujeto: Into the room walked a tall man.

hint.es: Lugar primero, luego el verbo y al final el sujeto.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es correcta cuando el sujeto es un pronombre?

choices.text: Down the hill ran it.
Down the hill it ran.
Down ran it the hill.

feedback.es: Con un pronombre no hay inversión: Down the hill it ran. Ran it y el orden roto no son inglés.

hint.es: Con pronombre, el verbo no se adelanta.

answer.text: had

feedback.es: Never al inicio pide inversión: never + auxiliar + sujeto, es decir, Never had I felt.

hint.es: Es el auxiliar del pasado perfecto y va antes del sujeto.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el recurso que usa.

pairs: Under the bed lay a small key.
Never had he felt so alone.

feedback.es: Cada frase usa un recurso: lugar + verbo + nombre, lugar + pronombre, never + inversión y fragmentos.

pairs: Under the bed lay a small key.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige quién viene primero calle abajo.

choices.text: A small dog.
A tall woman.

feedback.es: En «Down the street came a tall man» el sujeto va después del verbo: viene primero el hombre alto. El perro viene detrás.

prompt.es: Elige el párrafo con mejor ritmo: frase larga y una corta.

choices.text: The night was long and cold, and she waited for an hour for a bus that never came. Nothing.
The night was long and cold and dark and she waited and waited for the bus to come and nothing happened at all.
The night was long. It was cold. She waited. The bus did not come. Nothing.

feedback.es: Una frase larga que fluye seguida de una corta que golpea da ritmo. Una sola frase interminable o una serie de frases cortas y monótonas no.

prompt.es: Reescribe el párrafo con anteposición, never + inversión y dos fragmentos.

answer.text: Into the room walked a tall man. Down the hill ran the dog. Never had I seen such a silent night. Silence. Then footsteps.
accepted: Into the room walked a tall man. Down the hill ran the dog. Never had I seen such a silent night. Silence. Then footsteps.
In the doorway stood a tall man. Down the hill ran the dog. Never before had I seen such a silent night. Silence. Footsteps.

feedback.es: El párrafo mejora con lugar + verbo + sujeto (Into the room walked…), never + inversión (Never had I seen…) y fragmentos (Silence. Then footsteps.).

origin.text: Párrafo: «A tall man walked into the room. The dog ran down the hill. I had never seen such a silent night. There was silence. Then there were footsteps.» Reescríbelo con una anteposición de lugar con inversión, una frase con Never had y dos fragmentos sin verbo.

es: Reconstruir el orden real de los hechos en una anécdota que salta entre tiempos (past simple, past perfect, past perfect continuous, would) y sus marcadores.

teaching.en: By the time the last train arrived, my grandmother had been waiting on the platform for two hours.
teaching.es: Cuando llegó el último tren, mi abuela llevaba dos horas esperando en el andén.
teaching.explanationEs: Past perfect continuous (had been waiting): una actividad en curso antes del hecho principal.
segments: By the time the last train arrived, my grandmother
had been waiting on the platform for two hours.
teaching.audioText: By the time the last train arrived, my grandmother had been waiting on the platform for two hours.

teaching.en: Years earlier, her father had promised to take her to the city.

teaching.audioText: Years earlier, her father had promised to take her to the city.

teaching.en: Her cousin wasn't on the train, so she walked home alone.

segments: Her cousin wasn't on the train,
so she walked home alone.
teaching.audioText: Her cousin wasn't on the train, so she walked home alone.

teaching.en: A stranger gave her his umbrella, and they talked until the rain stopped.

segments: A stranger gave her his umbrella, and

teaching.en: She didn't know it then, but she would marry him three years later.

teaching.explanationEs: Would + verbo: anticipa algo posterior al momento del relato, visto desde el pasado.
segments: She didn't know it then, but she
would marry him three years later.
teaching.audioText: She didn't know it then, but she would marry him three years later.

teaching.en: An hour earlier, the man at the station had told her the train was late.

had told her the train was late.

prompt.es: Escribe una anécdota de unas 130 palabras con escena, giro y desenlace.

answer.text: It was a cold night, and the rain was falling on the roof of the bus station. The waiting room was almost empty, and a tired man was sleeping on a bench. I was about to buy a ticket when I realised my wallet was gone. Suddenly, my hands began to tremble. I was going to call my brother, but then a stranger walked over and handed me some money. "Take it," he said. "You can pay me back tomorrow." I thanked him and took the last bus home. Little did I know that I would see him again. The following week, he walked into my first job interview. He was the manager, and he would become my boss for the next five years.
accepted: It was a cold night, and the rain was falling on the roof of the bus station. The waiting room was almost empty, and a tired man was sleeping on a bench. I was about to buy a ticket when I realised my wallet was gone. Suddenly, my hands began to tremble. I was going to call my brother, but then a stranger walked over and handed me some money. "Take it," he said. "You can pay me back tomorrow." I thanked him and took the last bus home. Little did I know that I would see him again. The following week, he walked into my first job interview. He was the manager, and he would become my boss for the next five years.

It was a rainy evening, and the wind was blowing hard outside the station. A few people were waiting quietly in the dark. I was about to get on the last bus when I realised my wallet was not in my bag. My heart was beating very fast. I was going to ask the driver for help, but a young woman gave me a ticket. "Don't worry," she said. "Buy me a coffee one day." I thanked her and sat by the window. Little did I know that I would meet her again. Two weeks later, she came into my new office, and she would become my best friend for the rest of my life.

prompt.es: Cuenta la anécdota (unas 140 palabras) y responde a las dos preguntas del público.

answer.text:
Every summer, the whole family used to meet at my grandmother's house. The kitchen smelled of coffee, and the relatives were all talking at once. My uncle Tom would always tell the same story about his first car. That year, he was about to start it again when a stranger walked into the garden. Nobody recognised him. Silence. Then my grandmother laughed and opened her arms. "It's Leo!" she said. He had been travelling for ten years, and nobody had known where he was. Little did we know that he would stay with us for the whole summer.
Did you recognise him? No, I didn't. I thought he was a neighbour.
What did your uncle say? Fair enough, he said. Tonight, for once, we'll hear a new story.
accepted:
Every summer, the whole family used to meet at my grandmother's house. The kitchen smelled of coffee, and the relatives were all talking at once. My uncle Tom would always tell the same story about his first car. That year, he was about to start it again when a stranger walked into the garden. Nobody recognised him. Silence. Then my grandmother laughed and opened her arms. "It's Leo!" she said. He had been travelling for ten years, and nobody had known where he was. Little did we know that he would stay with us for the whole summer.
Did you recognise him? No, I didn't. I thought he was a neighbour.
What did your uncle say? Fair enough, he said. Tonight, for once, we'll hear a new story.

When I was a child, we would all meet at my grandmother's house on Sundays. The kitchen smelled of bread, and the relatives were all laughing in the garden. My uncle Tom used to tell the same story about his first car. One Sunday, he was about to begin when a tall man walked into the garden. Nobody knew him. Silence. Then my grandmother smiled and opened her arms. "It's Leo," she said. He had been living abroad for ten years, and nobody had heard from him. Little did I know that he would become my best friend.
Did you know him? No, I didn't. I thought he was a friend of my uncle.
What did your uncle say? Honestly, he said nothing. He just hugged him.

feedback.es: Una buena versión abre con hábito o escena, rompe con un hecho o was about to, da el giro con had been o Little did we know y responde a las preguntas del público con respuestas cortas.

Después responde a dos preguntas del público: «Did you recognise him?» y «What did your uncle say?».
